## Trial `dynamic-route-exchange-ubuntu16__wQusrdM`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The core task outcome is well-supported: node1 and node2 exchange their private-network routes via iBGP over the shared transit link (confirmed Established sessions, PfxRcd=1, kernel FIB routes with proto bgp), and node3/node4 achieve end-to-end reachability, verified both before and after a full sequential restart of all four nodes. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was executed on all four nodes with boot-id proof and recovered state, though node1's BGP session required a manual vtysh re-entry after its own reboot before the persistence service was created and enabled — that service's fully automatic recovery was only directly observed on node2's subsequent reboot, not on a second reboot of node1. Hygiene is good; the one notable mutation (docker0 address cleanup) was a bounded, necessary fix for an address conflict rather than an unexplained or destructive change.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.850 | 72/14 (+10 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node1 and node2 learn each other's private network (192.168.13.0/24 and 192.168.24.0/24) through a routing protocol rather than manually entered routes
  - **Why:** iBGP (AS 65100) was configured between node1 and node2 over the 172.20.1.0/172.20.1.1 transit /31, each advertising its own private subnet via a BGP 'network' statement with next-hop-self. Direct evidence shows the session reaching Established state with PfxRcd=1 in both directions, and each node's kernel FIB carrying the peer's subnet with 'proto bgp' (not a manually entered static route). No static route was placed on node1 or node2 for the other's private network; only node3/node4 (ordinary Linux end hosts that do not speak BGP) received a static route to their own gateway, a reasonable exception since the routing-protocol requirement targets node1/node2. One caveat: after node1's own restart, the BGP session did not come back automatically and had to be manually re-entered via vtysh before the boot-persistence service (antrieb-bgp-config.service) was created; that service was verified to work automatically only on node2's subsequent reboot, not on a second reboot of node1, so full automatic post-reboot self-healing of the BGP session is confirmed for node2 but only inferred (not directly observed) for node1.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a0c95c5de9dc40e8`, `cmd-95b2a4f5fd9e4706`, `cmd-0d4b5181838e40a1`, `cmd-8ab4d1af819f4fa5`, `cmd-c17948ef4027475c`, `cmd-ddcb5a848f2b41dc`, `cmd-6614d8b8fb6240aa`, `cmd-f5392a338c2849e6`, `cmd-1327147c19634bc8`, `cmd-035e6ffb5c1c490f`, `cmd-a67c6bd5a5e343fa`, `cmd-318b18ed6e7d4d37`, `cmd-7377eee31ae74218`, `cmd-1944cf2c25494f99`, `cmd-7e2792e40c914afa`, `cmd-25744efe6afa48d2`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** node3 and node4 can reach each other across the two private networks via the dynamically learned route
  - **Why:** Bidirectional ping between node3 (192.168.13.2) and node4 (192.168.24.2) succeeded with 0% packet loss after BGP was Established, and reachability was re-verified after each of the four sequential node restarts (node3, node4, node1, node2), confirming the path remained functional through the BGP-learned route rather than a one-off manual test.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-919a2b30d75f48aa`, `cmd-a01b1c25cfae4785`, `cmd-408ee065f20e4d1f`, `cmd-e82875631ec14c02`, `cmd-a4df0d8440214814`, `cmd-0ec57dfcdaad4bb0`, `cmd-74e69c0ca4ff4a7d`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Command trace shows a coherent, purposeful sequence: read-only topology discovery (ARP/tcpdump), addressing of transit and private links, BGP configuration, persistence-unit creation, and a full one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes with boot-id proof and post-restart verification. The 'ip addr del 240.127.1.1/24 dev docker0; ip link set docker0 down' step on node1/node2 (cmd-a0c95c5de9dc40e8, cmd-95b2a4f5fd9e4706) is the one mutation whose root cause (why docker0's address was leaking ARP traffic onto eth1/eth2) is not explained in the trace, but it was a bounded, low-risk cleanup of an address conflict blocking the required interface addressing, and docker0 was already down at baseline per the before-prepare snapshot, so no new persistent risk was introduced. Two vtysh configuration attempts that failed on 'write memory' (cmd-f19a6345a9804b2c, cmd-ce4950d84de74c4a) were immediately corrected with working syntax and are not residue. No abandoned files, conflicting services, or unnecessary destructive actions were observed; the after-executor snapshot shows no unexpected failed-service or package-health regressions versus after-prepare beyond expected boot-id/socket/tmp-file churn from the mandated restarts.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-a0c95c5de9dc40e8`, `cmd-95b2a4f5fd9e4706`, `cmd-f19a6345a9804b2c`, `cmd-ce4950d84de74c4a`, `cmd-98c1170db0084ddb`, `cmd-a6a1968c4aa44425`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services`, `global:before_prepare:node2:failed-services`

### Comments and limitations

- Automatic (unattended) recovery of the BGP session across a reboot was directly observed only for node2; for node1 the session had to be manually re-established once before the antrieb-bgp-config.service was created, so full self-healing on a hypothetical future node1 reboot is inferred from configuration and node2's parallel behavior rather than directly proven by a second node1 restart.
- The root cause of the docker0 address (240.127.1.1/24) appearing on/interfering with eth1 and eth2 on node1/node2 was not diagnosed in the trace, only worked around; this is noted for completeness though it did not block or compromise the outcome.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.850; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
